Sharma (2016) DBH–height models for Ontario plantations and natural stands

Source: R/hd_sharma2016.R
hd_sharma2016.Rd

Vectorized implementation of the population-level individual-tree height–diameter models of Sharma (2016), fitted separately to trees grown in plantations and in natural stands in Ontario. Predicts total tree height (m) from DBH (cm), stand origin and three stand-level predictors: dominant stand height, basal area and stand density.

Usage

hd_sharma2016(DBH, species, variant, HDOM, BA, TPH, keep_model_id = FALSE)

Arguments

DBH

Numeric vector. Tree level. Diameter at breast height (1.3 m above ground), in cm. Must be >= 0.

species

Character vector. Tree level. NFI species codes (e.g. "PICE.MAR"; compact "PICEMAR" is accepted).

variant

Character vector. Plot level. Stand origin selecting the parameter set: "plantation" (regenerated by planting) or "natural" (natural stand). No default; recycled like the other inputs, so stands of both origins can be predicted in one call. NA gives NA height.

HDOM

Numeric vector. Plot level. Dominant stand height (m): "average height of dominant and codominant trees" in the plot (source "SHT", pp. 71-72). Must be > 0.

BA

Numeric vector. Plot level. Total stand basal area (m²/ha) of the plot (source "BA", pp. 71-72). The source does not state a minimum DBH for this total. Must be > 0.

TPH

Numeric vector. Plot level. Stand density (stems/ha), "calculated from the trees with dbh \(\geq\) 2.5 cm" (source "TPH", p. 71). Must be > 0.

keep_model_id

Logical. If TRUE, add column model_id ("sharma2016_natural" or "sharma2016_plantation").

Value

A tibble with column height (m) and, if keep_model_id = TRUE, model_id.

Details

Model scope (species coverage): jack pine (PINU.BAN), red pine (PINU.RES), black spruce (PICE.MAR) and white spruce (PICE.GLA), each with a plantation and a natural-stand parameter set. Fitted to Ontario permanent sample plots (400 m²); red pine plots are mostly in the southwest of the province, the other species cover the boreal region (p. 71).

Model form (eq. 4, p. 75; same form as Sharma and Parton 2007, see hd_sharmaparton2007()): $$H = 1.3 + \theta \, HDOM^{\delta} [1 - \exp(-\beta (TPH / BA)^{\phi} DBH)]^{\gamma}.$$

Height convention: total tree height; DBH measured at 1.3 m, so predicted height tends to 1.3 m as DBH tends to 0.

Population-level prediction: coefficients are the fixed effects of the mixed-effects fit (Table 3, p. 74), evaluated with the plot-level random effect on \(\theta\) set to zero (\(u = 0\)), as in Fig. 4 of the source. Plot-specific calibration with measured heights is not implemented.

Notes on the published coefficients:

  • As published, \(\phi\) is negative for red pine in natural stands, and \(\delta\) and \(\phi\) are negative for black spruce in natural stands (p. 75). For these, predicted height decreases slightly with TPH / BA (and, for natural black spruce, with HDOM).

  • \(\phi\) for white spruce plantations is blank in Table 3 (the only non-significant parameter, p. 75). It is set to 0 here, so the TPH / BA term drops out and BA and TPH do not affect that model.

  • Table 3 does not exactly reproduce the curves in Fig. 4 at large DBH (differences up to about 1.2 m at 40 cm); this function implements Table 3 as published.

Rows with NA in any input return NA height. Inputs outside the range of the fitting data for the species and stand origin (DBH, Table 2; BA, TPH and HDOM, Table 1; p. 72) are computed and reported in a single warning.

References

Sharma, M. (2016). Comparing height–diameter relationships of boreal tree species grown in plantations and natural stands. Forest Science, 62(1), 70–77. doi:10.5849/forsci.14-232

See also

hd_sharmaparton2007(), hd_model_registry(), get_hd_model_info()

Examples

hd_sharma2016(
  DBH = c(10, 20, 30),
  species = "PINU.RES",
  variant = c("plantation", "natural", "natural"),
  HDOM = 16, BA = 25, TPH = 2200
)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 1
#>   height
#>    <dbl>
#> 1   13.4
#> 2   15.0
#> 3   17.9

# Inside dplyr::mutate() with tree and plot data
trees <- data.frame(
  DBH = c(12, 25, 18),
  species = c("PICE.MAR", "PICE.GLA", "PINU.BAN"),
  origin = c("plantation", "natural", "natural"),
  HDOM = c(12, 18, 18), BA = c(22, 30, 30), TPH = c(3000, 2000, 2000)
)
dplyr::mutate(trees, hd_sharma2016(DBH, species, origin, HDOM, BA, TPH))
#>   DBH  species     origin HDOM BA  TPH   height
#> 1  12 PICE.MAR plantation   12 22 3000 10.09483
#> 2  25 PICE.GLA    natural   18 30 2000 17.43386
#> 3  18 PINU.BAN    natural   18 30 2000 17.65263
